question: Which states require an office-holder to resign to run for another office (resign-to-run laws), and which bar holding two offices at once, for example a city council seat and a state legislative seat, or a state legislative seat and a run for Congress? When a person wins the higher office, what happens to the lower seat: automatic vacancy, a required resignation by a date, or allowed dual holding? And how is the vacated local seat filled?
requestedBy: Climbing from council to president playtest thread, filed by the research intake thread

sourcesChecked.source: Climbing from council to president playtest (2026-09-22)
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Found that no code ends a council seat when its holder wins higher office; does not say what real law requires.

title: Holding one office while running for another
usableAnswer: Per state: whether a resign-to-run law exists and which offices it covers, the dual-office-holding or incompatibility rules between local, state and federal offices with citations, what happens to the lower seat on winning, and how that vacancy is filled.
whyItMatters: The climbing playtest found nothing that ends a council seat when its holder moves up, so a player can hold every rung at once. Resign-to-run and incompatibility rules decide whether climbing costs anything.
